title: Book Three · Chapter 88: Twelve from the Pile
story:
At the old-book stall, Leo goes straight to the one-yuan pile.

Ronan opens a thin story. There is writing near one picture. The cover is worn, but the words are clear.

“Ordinary stories,” the seller says. “No special old treasure here.”

Leo grins. “Good. We have ordinary money.”

They choose twelve books from the pile. Some are stories. A few have simple puzzles or travel pictures.

Ronan opens each one at the front and in the middle. Leo checks the covers and the loose corners.

They put two aside. One smells damp. Another has several pages loose at the back. They choose two others instead, so the pile still has twelve.

“Twelve yuan,” the seller says.

Ronan takes twelve from the shared forty. Leo counts the books once more before they pay.

There are twenty-eight yuan left.

At the next stall, they buy two strong secondhand cloth bags. Each costs one yuan. Both are plain and large enough for several thin books.

The bags cost two yuan together. Their shared cash is now twenty-six.

Ronan writes the two costs on his sheet. Leo holds the bags open while he puts the books inside.

On the walk home, Leo talks about the table.

“Near the pencil stall. People already stop there.”

“We need to ask.”

“I know. Not across the doorway.”

At home, they put the bought books beside their six old ones. Eighteen in all.

Mum looks over from her chair.

“Those bags need a wash before you keep books in them.”

They take the books out again. Ronan washes one bag at the yard tap. Leo washes the other. They hang them in the sun.

“Now the stock has a bath,” Leo says.

“Only its trousers.”

They laugh. Ronan gives each group of books a small paper mark. R for his three, L for Leo's three, B for the twelve they bought.

The letters will help them remember the sources. All eighteen are for the shared sale now.

Leo sits beside the pile and turns a travel book. A picture shows a boat larger than any boat Ronan has seen.

“We could sell these quickly,” Leo says.

“If people want them.”

“Then we need people.”

Ronan looks through the gate. Two customers are waiting at Mr Qiu's stall.

He puts the purchase sheet beside their shared money. Eighteen books and twenty-six yuan. The new football stays in the yard, and the blue bracelet moves against his wrist as he counts the last book.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

worn＝磨旧的；source＝来源；one yuan each＝每本一元；in all＝总共。

## 理解问题

1. 十二本书和两个袋子各花多少？共同现金最后剩多少？
2. 加上各自投入的旧书，现在总库存是多少？R、L、B分别表示什么？

## 读句子

**There are twenty-eight yuan left.**

拆开看：There are / twenty-eight yuan / left.

还有／二十八元／剩下。
